title: Setting straight the ocean crossings and cruises
summary: He corrects claims he played 22 crossings; most trips were with his parents, with only the Republic, Pennland and one Caribbean cruise on the Mauritania.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Uh-huh. In addition to your Atlantic crossings, John Chilton mentions that you also crossed the Mediterranean and cruised to South America. Is that right?

Well, I was on a Mediterranean cruise in 1926 with my parents, at the conclusion of which we visited Paris and London, but I did play on a Caribbean cruise on the old Mauritania, the old four stacker.
Was that the only one towards South America?
I see. Okay. And Leonard Feather mentions in his encyclopedia that you crossed the ocean 22 times, later went to the South Seas and Latin America. Is that a good count?
Well, I don't know. I'm glad it's an even number, because I couldn't have gotten back where I was.
That speaks for its accuracy, then.

I think that's a little exagerarrated, because, let's see, there's two, four -- I'm thinking of the Republic and the Pennland. Of course I did travel with my parents quite a bit on some of these trips.
I see. Because the implication is that -- he doesn't actually say so, though, but the implication is that you were playing all those trips.
Well, this is another one of those things, over a period of time that becomes -- like you say, it doesn't say so, but it winds up meaning that.
